summary: Couch Investor covers four quality companies amid a red tape for semis (Nvidia -2%, Micron -4.3%, AMD -2.7%) and a ~70% market-implied chance of a Fed rate hike the following week, with the 10-year at 4.92% and the ECB hiking to 2.5%. Zeta Global is up 55% YTD yet he calls it a very good accumulation zone: $7.7B market cap, forward P/E 28.3, PEG under 1, revenue per employee and margins trending up, his DCF slightly undervalued, and the Palantir partnership's growth acceleration not yet priced — it needn't become a $100B company, just $10-20B. Shopify, down 19.4% YTD at $163B, is expensive (trailing P/E 85, forward 60) but excellently managed and AI-native; the Meta Muse selloff was misread because agents will shop on Shopify stores, which provide the backend, security, and payments. Palantir, flat YTD at ~$400B and forward P/E ~88, is 'the special company' — accelerating growth, revenue per employee up 62.9% YoY, operating margin expanding, 84.8% gross margin, ~49% net margin, 54.6% free cash flow margin; he owns it from $107. AMD, up 126% YTD to over $820B, is pricey versus Nvidia ($5.2T) but its real growth acceleration is around the corner with the MI400/MI500 Helios ramp, and it could become a $1-2T company on execution. Calls: AMD BUY; PLTR BUY; ZETA BUY.
